SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which county borders Uganda? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Nyeri
   C. Busia
   D. Kitui

2. Which country lies to the west of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Somalia
   B. Uganda
   C. Tanzania
   D. Ethiopia

3. Why is it useful to know the size of a county? (1 mark)
   A. It tells us the price of food
   B. It tells us what to eat
   C. It tells us the weather
   D. It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics

4. On a county sketch map, what does the north arrow show? (1 mark)
   A. The size of the county
   B. The direction of north
   C. The rainfall
   D. The number of people

5. Which physical feature is best for building roads, towns and farms easily? (1 mark)
   A. A plain
   B. A deep valley
   C. A waterfall
   D. A steep mountain

6. In many parts of Kenya, when do the short rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. January only
   B. March to May
   C. October to December
   D. June to July

7. Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The coast
   B. A low dry plain
   C. The slopes of Mount Kenya
   D. A beach

8. Which of these is a service learning activity at a historic site? (1 mark)
   A. Sweeping and collecting litter
   B. Building a fire
   C. Selling tickets to friends
   D. Painting graffiti

9. What is trade? (1 mark)
   A. Playing games
   B. Growing crops only
   C. Building houses
   D. Buying and selling goods

10. On a timeline, which event comes first? (1 mark)
   A. The biggest event
   B. The newest event
   C. The funniest event
   D. The oldest event

11. Why must children not do hard or dangerous work? (1 mark)
   A. It is fun
   B. It harms their health and schooling
   C. It is a school rule
   D. It makes them stronger

12. What does jua kali mean in Kiswahili? (1 mark)
   A. Cold wind
   B. Rainy day
   C. Hot sun
   D. Big factory

13. Which of these can be a school enterprise project? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. A robbery
   C. A war
   D. A vegetable garden

14. What is a budget? (1 mark)
   A. A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   B. A crop
   C. A type of tool
   D. A game

15. Which action shows cooperation? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing tasks in a group
   B. Copying others
   C. Fighting
   D. Doing nothing

16. Which action shows cleanliness? (1 mark)
   A. Putting litter in the bin
   B. Spitting in class
   C. Writing on walls
   D. Throwing rubbish on the ground

17. What is cyberbullying? (1 mark)
   A. Playing a computer game
   B. Reading a book
   C. Writing a letter
   D. Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone

18. What does punctuality mean? (1 mark)
   A. Running fast
   B. Arriving late
   C. Arriving on time
   D. Speaking loudly

19. What is a conflict? (1 mark)
   A. A holiday
   B. A book
   C. A song
   D. A disagreement or quarrel

20. What is the first step in solving a conflict peacefully? (1 mark)
   A. Run away
   B. Hit
   C. Shout
   D. Stop and calm down

21. What does fairness mean? (1 mark)
   A. Favouring friends
   B. Favouring rich people
   C. Treating everyone equally
   D. Ignoring people

22. What is female genital mutilation? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   B. A kind of food
   C. A kind of sport
   D. A kind of school

23. At what age can a Kenyan vote in national elections? (1 mark)
   A. 18 years
   B. 10 years
   C. 15 years
   D. 12 years

24. What should you do if your candidate loses? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Fight
   C. Refuse to work with the winner
   D. Accept the results peacefully

25. What does majority mean? (1 mark)
   A. No votes
   B. The smaller number of votes
   C. A tie
   D. The larger number of votes

26. Which minister would deal with dirty toilets? (1 mark)
   A. Library
   B. Sports
   C. Music
   D. Health and sanitation

27. Which shows respect for the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Following fair instructions politely
   B. Insulting leaders
   C. Laughing at them
   D. Ignoring leaders

28. What does a patron do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives the bus
   B. Cooks for pupils
   C. Wins all elections
   D. Guides and advises the pupil leaders

29. Who leads the meetings of the assembly of pupils? (1 mark)
   A. The gatekeeper
   B. The cook
   C. The Speaker
   D. The driver

30. What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by? (1 mark)
   A. Foreign governments
   B. County governments
   C. Private banks only
   D. The army

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. What does the Kiswahili word amani mean and why is it important in a school? (2 marks)

32. Explain why many families live near towns and rivers. (3 marks)

33. Name the two main parts of a county government and state what each does. (4 marks)

34. Name two water features found in Kenya. (2 marks)

35. State the direction that is opposite to each of these: north and east. (2 marks)

36. Describe four steps to develop a good quality such as punctuality. (4 marks)

37. Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date. (5 marks)

38. Give two reasons why we need to know the location of our county. (2 marks)

39. What is meant by a densely populated area? (2 marks)

40. Explain three ways in which a county can benefit when its officers know its size and location well. (3 marks)

41. State three reasons why Kenya has county governments. (3 marks)

42. Explain why early marriage is against the rights of a child. (5 marks)

43. Name four members of a typical Children's Government. (4 marks)

44. Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs. (3 marks)

45. Describe how you would make a poster on an economic activity in your county. (4 marks)

46. Explain the meaning of a good citizen in school. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Busia
   Busia is on the border with Uganda.

2. B — Uganda
   Uganda is Kenya's western neighbour.

3. D — It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   Planners need to know how much land there is to cover with services.

4. B — The direction of north
   A north arrow shows which way is north so the map can be read correctly.

5. A — A plain
   Flat land is easy to build on and farm.

6. C — October to December
   The short rains usually come between October and December.

7. C — The slopes of Mount Kenya
   High places are colder than low places.

8. A — Sweeping and collecting litter
   Cleaning up is a way of serving and conserving.

9. D — Buying and selling goods
   Trade is buying and selling.

10. D — The oldest event
   Timelines run from oldest to newest.

11. B — It harms their health and schooling
   Child labour is harmful and against the law.

12. C — Hot sun
   Jua kali means hot sun, from workers who work outdoors.

13. D — A vegetable garden
   A garden can be run safely by pupils.

14. A — A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   A budget plans money.

15. A — Sharing tasks in a group
   Cooperation is working well with others.

16. A — Putting litter in the bin
   Using bins keeps the school clean.

17. D — Using phones or computers to hurt or frighten someone
   Cyberbullying is bullying online.

18. C — Arriving on time
   Punctual people arrive on time.

19. D — A disagreement or quarrel
   A conflict is a disagreement.

20. D — Stop and calm down
   We must calm down before talking.

21. C — Treating everyone equally
   Fair people give everyone equal treatment.

22. A — Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   FGM harms girls and is against the law.

23. A — 18 years
   Adults aged 18 and above can vote.

24. D — Accept the results peacefully
   Accepting results is part of democracy.

25. D — The larger number of votes
   Majority means more than others.

26. D — Health and sanitation
   Health and sanitation looks after cleanliness.

27. A — Following fair instructions politely
   Respect includes obeying fair instructions.

28. D — Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   The patron is a teacher adviser.

29. C — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads meetings.

30. B — County governments
   Pre-primary education is a county function.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Amani means peace. It is important because pupils feel safe and can learn well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 mark for the reason.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Towns have jobs, schools and shops. Rivers give water for drinking and farming. These things make life easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for towns, 1 mark for rivers, 1 mark for making life easier.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: The county executive runs the county and carries out laws. The county assembly makes county laws and checks the executive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part and 1 mark for each job.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lake Victoria and the Tana River. Accept Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha or the Indian Ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct feature.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: The opposite of north is south. The opposite of east is west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct opposite.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the quality, set a small goal, practise every day, and ask a friend to encourage you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: To plan journeys and to know which counties are next to us. Accept sharing resources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: An area where many people live close together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many people, 1 mark for close together.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: They can plan roads and health centres to reach people. They can share resources with neighbours. They can plan journeys and services better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: To bring services closer to people, to let people take part in decisions, and to share development fairly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: It stops a child from going to school. It harms health. It takes away childhood and play. It is against the law because the age of marriage is 18. It limits the child's future.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: President, deputy president, Speaker, and class representatives. Accept cabinet members or secretary.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each member.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct row.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose one activity, draw a large picture showing people at work, write a title and two or three facts, and add one way of conserving the resource.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A good citizen in school follows the rules, respects others and does what is good for the whole school community.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rules/respect, 1 mark for the community idea.
